In **2005–06 season** **[Associazione Calcio Milan](AC_Milan "AC Milan")** had a rather modest season compared to its previous seasons, before being rocked by a minor involvement in the [2006 Italian football scandal](2006_Italian_football_scandal "2006 Italian football scandal"), where rivals [Juventus](Juventus_F.C. "Juventus F.C.") was relegated and stripped of two league titles. Due to Milan's involvement, it did not inherit either of the titles, instead being penalised and dropped down the 2006 order, initially out of European football but later reinstated into fourth, which meant [UEFA Champions League](UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") qualification, a tournament Milan then went on to [win](2006%E2%80%9307_UEFA_Champions_League "2006–07 UEFA Champions League"). However, Milan started the 2006–07 Serie A season with an eight-point deduction, which complicated hopes of a new league title.

On the pitch, Milan was not able to challenge Juventus for the virtual league title, then going out against [Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") in the Champions League.

Following the season, the club sold [Andriy Shevchenko](Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") for €40 million, the highest fee paid for a player turning 30 in the same year, to English club [Chelsea](Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.").
